reasoning_traces.think:
The core tension lies between pooled weight (PW) and information-covariance integration (ICI) fusion methods. PW assumes zero cross-covariance among sources, which leads to inconsistent estimates and overconfidence when sources are actually correlated. This manifests in lower Sharpe ratios (0.11 vs 0.48) and underestimation of risk. ICI, by contrast, incorporates full covariance structure, enabling more accurate inference. The failure mode of PW is mathematically characterized by its inability to model off-diagonal terms in the precision matrix, resulting in a singular point estimate. In GSE, this translates to over-trust in correlated signals, which can be mitigated using structured covariance-aware fusion. The dual nature of these estimators reflects a fundamental duality in ensemble theory: one based on scalar variance (PW) versus matrix-valued information (ICI). The breakdown regime occurs when source dependencies exceed the independence assumption of PW. Empirical verification shows that ICI consistently outperforms PW in both Sharpe ratio and log-loss metrics, confirming its superiority in correlated environments.
